abstract: Transparency in AI-supported decision systems is widely required but poorly defined. Existing approaches treat transparency as a property of systems or components, producing characteristic failures: assessments that do not transfer across organizational boundaries, stakeholder questions that cannot be formulated within the available frame of analysis, and component-level findings that say nothing about system-level behavior. We propose treating transparency as a relation: a system is transparent to a stakeholder to the degree that their legitimate questions are answerable from its structure. We formalize this using information flow networks, in which transparency questions are expressed in terms of network structure and answerability is the condition that the system settles them. The framework supports three dimensions of analysis: structural answerability from the network alone, compositional answerability across organizational boundaries for deployed systems, and role-dependent answerability given a stakeholder's accessible sub-network. We demonstrate the framework on a real pre-integration assessment of an AI recruitment tool in a public sector municipality. The assessment uses participatory design and interviews to model the decision system structure. We show how structural and role-dependent transparency questions can be formally stated and analyzed across the Provider and Deployer boundary where the AI system is composed together with the deployer's decision process.

ob.tldr: 透明度在AI决策系统中被广泛要求却缺乏统一定义。研究将透明度重新界定为关系属性——系统对某利益相关者透明的程度取决于其合法问题能否从系统结构中得到回答。基于信息流网络提出形式化框架，支持结构性、跨组织边界的可组合性、角色依赖三类分析，并在某公共部门AI招聘工具的预集成评估中通过参与式设计与访谈进行实证。

title: Transparency as Answerability: Role-Dependent Information Flow Modeling
title_zh: 透明性即可问责性：角色相关的信息流建模
